blocks.text: The Berlin Left Party, Greens and SPD are to meet to clarify controversial issues ahead of possible coalition talks. The second fuel tax cut this year has come into force as gas and diesel prices spiral. DW has more.

blocks.caption: The Left Party's Elif Eralp is poised to be Berlin's first governing mayorImage: Emmanuele Contini/NurPhoto/picture alliance

items: The Left Party, the Greens and the Social Democrats (SPD) in Berlin are to test the ground for a possible coalition
Talks will center on accusations that the Left Party is antisemitic and has links to organized criminality, which it denies
A fuel tax cut aiming to reduce costs for motorists goes into effect for the second time this year

blocks.text: Here is a rundown of the stories from and about Germany that are hitting the headlines on Thursday, October 1, 2026:
Sahra Wagenknecht Alliance changes its name

blocks.caption: Sahra Wagenknecht's name has been dropped from the title of the party she foundedImage: Andreas Gora/IMAGO

blocks.text: The populist Sahra Wagenknecht Alliance (BSW) has officially dropped its founder's name from its title to become the Alliance for Social Justice and Economic Reason.
However, it will retain the abbreviation BSW.
Secretary general Oliver Ruhnert said Wagenknecht's name had initially been used because of her popularity but that the party had now succeeded in establishing itself as a brand in its own right.
Wagenknecht, a former parliamentary leader of the Left Party, founded the BSW in 2024, stepping down as its leader in November 2025.

Although the BSW advocates economic policies that are left-wing, it also has a nationalist and anti-migration stance that are more typical of the right-wing political spectrum, making it hard to classify in conventional terms.
It also favors closer ties with Russia.
